note: Lanes of the stability lab (plans/cmux-next/chrome-parity/p10-stability.md, section 3.A). stability-lab.py reads id and tier; the runner (task 003) reads the rest. Every lane runs through cmux-ci at the lowest priority, never on a bench host, and blocks no push, merge or nightly.

lanes.summary: cargo-fuzz, 5 minutes per cmux-tui/fuzz target, each from its stored corpus; the run's corpus is minimized (-merge=1) and stored back.

corpus.carry: {corpus_in} is the cmux-tui family's carried store, a packed store (fuzz-corpus.py export) uploaded for the step's lane with `cmux-ci artifact-put`. A rust-fuzz or rust-fuzz-coverage step updates it when rust-fuzz.sh exited with one of carry_exit_codes and wrote its artifact, whatever the lane's verdict: exit 1 is a finding, and that run's corpus is valid (`cmux-ci artifact --failed` takes its artifact). Exit 75 or no artifact leaves the carry as it was. The update is merge-on-write, one step at a time in the runner: carry_merge packs the union of the current carry and the step's store ({step_artifact}) as {corpus_next}, which becomes the next {corpus_in}. So two overlapping steps that started from one carry keep each other's finds, whichever finishes last (test_fuzz_corpus.py, LaneCarry). Each update is a new store object (objects live 14 days), so an open crash never lets the carry expire. The step's --store is a fresh directory in its checkout, so the corpus moves with the lane, not with the host. With no carry yet the lane drops --store-import and starts from the seeds.

lanes.findings: summary.jsonl verdicts crash, oom, timeout and leak; each artifact goes through crash_signature.py and stability_issues.py. The fix commits `rust-fuzz.sh --minimize-crash TARGET FILE`, a regression input of at most 64 KiB under cmux-tui/fuzz/corpus/<target>/.

lanes.summary: cargo fuzz coverage + llvm-cov of every target's stored corpus; covered regions go into the store's history, and a target flat over its last 3 measurements gets one fuzz-quality issue.

corpus.carry: the same carry as rust-fuzz, updated the same way (merge-on-write), so a coverage step that overlaps a fuzz step keeps the fuzz step's growth; its store carries the coverage history to the next run.
